queries.text: "sem o temor de impressioná-la" literally "without the fear of impressing her"; probably "without worrying about (failing to) impress her" or "without fear of shocking her". Kept the literal reading.

Schopenhauer (2004, a Portuguese anthology on women) translated from the author’s Portuguese; the passage is from “The Metaphysics of Love of the Sexes,” whose public-domain English version is R. B. Haldane and J. Kemp’s (The World as Will and Idea, vol. III).
